newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open flat to weaker.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open flat to weaker.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were called to open flat to weaker Friday as dealers continued to seek the implications of Germany's central bank gold revaluation plan to help qualify for European economic and monetary union.
COMEX June gold was called off $0.50 to $1.00 from Thursday's close of $348.40 an ounce after trading from $348.80 to $347.50 on ACCESS.
COMEX July silver was called 1.00 to 2.00 cents weaker after trading from $4.865 to $4.85 on ACCESS.
Many of Europe's central banks said they had no plans to reevaluate their own gold reserves.
London gold fixed a touch higher Friday morning at $347.00, up $0.60 from Thursday afternoon.
COMEX gold stocks on Thursday fell 1,447 ounces to 895,028 ounces, while the exchange's silver stocks rose 812,260 ounces to 191,875,292 ounces.
NYMEX July platinum was called flat to off $0.50 from yesterday's close of $393.90 an ounce, with NYMEX June palladium called unchanged.
